Subject: Redwood private install — initial preflight

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the quick intro. We're starting preflight for a single-tenant private deployment in our US-East colo (equinix), and want to lock down cluster and storage choices before procurement. High level constraints:
- 4 production GPUs with predictable latency for real-time queries (no bursty background jobs on same nodes)
- Models: mix of 30B-70B, expecting many quantized variants; we want local shard caching to avoid pulling large weights from network on pod start
- 10 TB of persistent model artifacts, ~4 TB hot cache expected; logs/metrics sent to our ELK stack (separate network)
- Strict egress controls, MTU=9000 preferred, and we use on-prem KMS for keys

Can you send a concise node/storage plan and any preflight checks we should run? I'll attach our internal preflight checklist.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure, Neotech Systems

Subject: Re: Redwood private install — initial preflight

Sarah — thanks, appreciate the checklist. Quick reply with a concise recommended plan (see below) and a few clarifying questions. We'll schedule a 60m design review once you confirm constraints.

Summary recommendation (high-level):
- Cluster: 3 worker classes (control-plane separate):
  * gpu-rt (4 x H100/A100 equivalent, reserved; low-latency, no background workloads)
  * gpu-batch (2-4 burst nodes for offline work; preemptible OK)
  * infra (registry, monitoring, routing)
- Storage: three tiers:
  1) local NVMe (ephemeral) per GPU node for KV/prefix caches and model shard hot cache (~1-2 TB NVMe per node)
  2) durable SSD-backed PVs (block storage via CSI) for model artifacts that need persistence across reboots (~4-8 TB pool, ReadWriteMany not required)
  3) archival object store (S3-compatible) for cold model versions and backups
- Networking: MTU 9000, dedicated subnet for model traffic, default egress to customer firewall; L4 LB with client-proxied TLS termination (we avoid nodePort on GPU nodes)
- Security: integrate with your KMS for model encryption keys; workload identities via mTLS and short-lived certs; audit logging to your ELK (syslog/Fluentd)

Clarifying questions:
1) Preferred GPU family? (H100 80GB preferred for 70B inference; if A100 is chosen need to plan for larger model sharding)
2) Do you require ReadWriteMany for model PVs (several pods mounting same model directory) or will each pod keep a local copy?
3) Expected QPS and 99th-pct latency SLO so we can size CPU and NICs appropriately.

I'll attach a one-page node sizing csv and a network diagram for your ops team. Next steps: Laura will lead the network gating checklist; Priyom will propose PVC classes and binding modes.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: node-sizing-proposal.csv, neotech-network-diagram-v2.pdf

Aditya / team — quick answers inline: 
- GPU family: we prefer A100 80GB (existing inventory) but can evaluate H100 if latency benefits justify cost.
- PV pattern: prefer local copy per pod for fastest access; central durable store for model publishing and rollback.
- Expected steady-state QPS: 120 reqs/sec (p50 ~12ms, p99 target <180ms). Burst up to 300/s for short windows.

Also: compliance ask — we need to preserve model access audit trails for 12 months. We plan to forward access events to ELK with RBAC mapping.

-Markus
Markus Holt

Subject: Fwd: Redwood private install — initial preflight

Team — forwarding Neotech thread. Key dimensioning notes based on their replies: QPS ~120 steady, p99 <180ms, prefer A100 80GB, local-copy per pod, 12m audit retention to ELK.

My proposed technical actions (internal):
- Node sizing: gpu-rt nodes: 4 x A100-80GB (1 GPU per node vs 2 per node depends on QPS isolation). Propose 2 pods per GPU for headroom; CPU per GPU 16 cores, 64GB RAM, NIC 100Gbps (enable SR-IOV where available).
- Disk layout: 2 TB NVMe local for hot cache + 500GB NVMe for OS; separate SSD pool (4TB) presented via CSI as PVs for persistent model store. Use local-pv for the NVMe cache (Local Persistent Volumes) and ensure the scheduler respects node-affinity.
- PVC binding: use WaitForFirstConsumer for model PVs that should land on GPU nodes; avoid dynamic RWX unless customer confirms. Priyom, can you draft StorageClass YAMLs and a local-pv binder recipe?
- Kubelet eviction thresholds: set nodefs.available at 5%, imagefs at 6% and enable evictions for imagefs to prevent OOM/killing inference pods. Document podPriority for infra vs real-time pods.
- Network: validate MTU 9000 path end-to-end; propose dedicated VLAN for model traffic. Soojin, assign checklist items for firewall rules and load balancer connectivity (no public egress from GPU nodes).

I will pull a draft playbook and send to Sarah/Markus by EOD 4/6.

Laura Bennett
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah / Markus — attaching the concise preflight playbook and node-sizing CSV. Below are the agreed action items and timeline.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Finalize GPU family (A100 vs H100) — Neotech (Markus) — 2026-04-09
- Network gating checks (MTU, VLANs, firewall rules) — Redwood (Soojin) — 2026-04-08
- StorageClass + LocalPV binder + WaitForFirstConsumer YAMLs — Redwood (Priyom) — 2026-04-06 (draft sent, see attachment)
- Audit forwarding config to ELK (syslog/Fluentd templates) — Neotech (Sarah) & Redwood (Laura) — 2026-04-10
- Procurement BOM draft (racks, NICs, NVMe sizes) — Neotech ops — 2026-04-12

Notes / Technical summary highlights:
- Local NVMe caches significantly reduce model load latency; expect cold-start improvement from tens of seconds to ~2-4s when cache warm. Plan for 2 TB per GPU node for hot shards given 4 TB hot footprint across cluster.
- Use WaitForFirstConsumer binding for durable model PVs to ensure PV scheduling onto GPU nodes when necessary; avoid RWX unless explicitly required.
- KMS integration: Redwood will accept key-encryption via your HSM-backed KMS; we will not persist decrypted artifacts outside container process.
- Audit: enable request-level audit logging for model loads + inference requests; forward to ELK with 12-month retention (customer side).

Attachments: neotech-preflight-playbook.pdf, node-sizing-proposal.csv (draft), neotech-network-diagram-v2.pdf
